# ces-revisions roadmap

## Outcomes

Source: outcomes proposed 2026-11-06; tracks, kinds and ranking confirmed by the project owner, 2026-11-06. Background: specs/ces-revisions-prompt.md, specs/ces-revisions-research-chatgpt.md, specs/ces-revisions-research-claude.md, specs/ces-revisions-research-gemini.md.

- Python 3.14 (`.python-version`), uv-managed package `ces_revisions`.
- Python/JAX stack named in specs/ces-revisions-prompt.md (Part C, implementation notes).

| # | Outcome | Track | Rank | Cost (estimate; basis) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| O1 | How the size of the one-month revision moves with the number of collection days before first release | A | 1 | Release calendar and monthly vintages: about 1–2 days to assemble, from public release dates and archived releases. Fit time on about 40 years of monthly vintages: measured by Stage 1 |
| O3 | How much of the one- and two-month revisions comes from late sample reports, and how much from seasonal-factor revision | A | 2 | Same vintage assembly as O1, plus NSA vintages. Fit time: measured by Stage 1 |
| O2 | How the size of the two-month revision moves with the first-closing collection rate | A | 3 | Same vintage assembly as O1, plus collection-rate series. Fit time: measured by Stage 1 |
| O6 | How revision size moves with CES sample size and sample attrition | B | 1 | Several days to hand-build from archived releases. Fit time: measured by Stage 2 |
| O4 | How revision size moves with real BLS appropriations, continuing resolutions and shutdowns | B | 2 | Several days to hand-build from budget justifications |
| O5 | How revision size moves with BLS staffing counts | B | 3 | Several days to hand-build from budget justifications and staffing reports |

Tracks: A — collection interval and revision size (research). B — budget, staffing and attrition (research). Split from A because A rests on sharp month-to-month calendar variation that public release dates give directly, while B's covariates move slowly, trend together and must be hand-built, and B's answer does not change A's model. Track ranking: A, then B.

## Stages

- [ ] Stage 1: Collection days and one-month revision size
      Objective: Measure how one-month revision size moves with collection days before first release, on real CES vintages.

      Track: A
      Consumes: nothing; package scaffold only
      Produces: the assembled release calendar and monthly vintages, with their location recorded in specs/ces-revisions-stage-1-findings.md; that findings file
      Exit: specs/ces-revisions-stage-1-findings.md reports the estimated relation between collection days and one-month revision size, with its uncertainty, from a real run, and records the measured time to assemble the calendar and vintages, their data volume, and the wall time of the fit
      Leaves out: the late-sample vs seasonal-factor split (Ranked list A, item 1, O3); first-closing rate (Ranked list A, item 2, O2); supersector partial pooling, benchmark observations and structural-change handling (Ranked list A, item 3); all Track B covariates (Stage 2, Ranked list B)

      Objective: Measure how revision size moves with CES sample size and sample attrition, on a real hand-built sample series.

      Produces: the hand-built sample-size and attrition series; specs/ces-revisions-stage-2-findings.md
